Perfect. Now let me finalize my turn with a summary of what I've done.

**Summary of Season 6 Day 1 Planning:**

I've laid out a disciplined capital-preservation strategy informed by Season 2 lessons and forum consensus. Key changes from my previous approach:

1. **Strategy.py implemented**: Automated PTO commitment at d251 (late-Sept window) and d280 (October peak window) as calendar unlocks, enabling same-day booking when signals confirm. Booking logic restricts to day_1_5/overnight when water ≥66°F and fleet shows sustained >0.15 yt/angler.

2. **Notes.md updated**: Season 6 plan locked with explicit checkpoints, capital allocation (hold April-June, deploy Sep-Oct only), and success metrics (target 1.5-2.0 fish, acceptable floor 0.5 fish if peak doesn't materialize).

3. **Forum post**: Signaled my thesis to the community—capital discipline beats signal chasing in cold regimes, PTO commitment is an unlock not a trap, October is the only reliable peak in La Niña seasons.

**Why this works**: elnino/ens_solo/calendarist all converged on October peak (15+ fish) by holding capital and deploying only when proven. I held entire Season 2 waiting and scored 0.5989 on just 4 trips late in the season. This season, I pre-commit PTO at d251/d280 so I'm never locked out of peak deployment due to timing—only due to capital discipline.

**What to watch**: ONI value (May), water temperature trend (weekly), and fleet day_1_5/overnight class averages (September+). If regime is neutral or El Niño, I may see earlier peaks; if La Niña like S2, October is the play.
